description:
FILED s444 from agent F (s443f) probes; PRE-EXISTING, unqualified too (not #491).  fileno on a CLOSED or never-opened bareword handle returns -1; perl returns undef.  `open(W,">",$f); close(W); defined(fileno(W))` -> perl undef, PCL [-1].  Same family as #220 (closed-handle value) and #403 (defined-but-false filetest).  Bar: closed / never-opened / open (inverse) vs perl; a punct-array-glob-01.t or io row.
--- DONE s448n (Opus round-6 agent N), commit 4437396 ---

perl has TWO negative answers and they are DIFFERENT FACTS (probed 5.40.3, all
seventeen shapes): **undef** when the handle is not open -- never opened,
closed, an empty lexical, a closed glob, a closed handle NAME in a scalar --
and **-1** only for an OPEN in-memory (scalar) handle, which has no descriptor
to name.  PCL answered -1 to both.

Consequence found while fixing it: `IO::Handle::opened` in lib/IO/Handle.pm is
literally `defined fileno($_[0])`, so it could never say no.

%p-fileno-impl asks `open-stream-p` before it asks for a descriptor.  A
DIRHANDLE keeps answering -1 (perl gives the real dirfd, PCL has none, and -1
preserves the definedness perl's callers test) -- that is a deliberate
non-change, not an oversight.

Bar met: closed / never-opened / open, bareword AND lexical AND glob AND glob
ref AND name-in-a-scalar, plus the in-memory pair and the three standard
handles, all identical to perl.  Gate 178/6007 PASS; sweep TOTAL 18321,
unchanged by this commit.  Guard Pl/t/std-handle-open-01.t rows 6-7 (the real
fd is folded to "fd": its NUMBER is not perl's, since SBCL holds descriptors of
its own, and the number is not what the rows are about).
